title: The Right Wing of the SABR Smile with an Absorbing Boundary: Resolution of Conjectures of Henry-Labordère
abstract: We determine the fixed-maturity right tail of the SABR model with $β\in(0,1)$ absorbed at zero, for every correlation $ρ$: the probability $P(k)$ that the forward ends above $f_0e^k$ satisfies $-k^{-2}\ln P(k)\to(1-β)^2/(2ν^2T(1-(ρ\wedge0)^2))$. The implied volatility therefore tends to $ν\sqrt{1-(ρ\wedge0)^2}/(1-β)$. Henry-Labordère's conjectured limit $ν/(1-β)$, which Hagan's leading-order formula also gives, holds for $ρ\ge0$ and fails for $ρ<0$, where survival keeps the noise orthogonal to volatility above a moving square-root barrier. The Gaussian estimate behind his second conjecture does not hold for $ρ<0$; the rate is instead given by the intrinsic distance within the survival domain.
comment: v2: adds a comparison with Hagan's formula and shorter proofs for nonnegative correlation; states the saddle-point value of the potential (Section 6.4) as a large-strike limit rather than a constant; minor corrections; revised exposition. 38 pages, 4 figures

bite.hook: Proves that Henry-Labordère's famous volatility formula fails for negative correlations, resolving open mathematical conjectures.
tldr: Determined the fixed-maturity right tail of the SABR model with absorption at zero for any correlation parameter.
Derived explicit probability limits and implied volatility behaviors using intrinsic distances within survival domains.
Found that Henry-Labordère's conjectured limit holds for non-negative correlations but fails when correlation is negative.
bite.whyItMatters: The SABR model is a cornerstone of modern quantitative finance for pricing interest rate and equity derivatives. Correcting its mathematical limits ensures traders do not misprice financial options under negative market correlations.
bite.eli5: Imagine a weather prediction rule that works great when wind and rain move together, but completely falls apart when the wind blows backward. Mathematicians just figured out the exact hidden math rule that fixes the formula for when things move in opposite directions.
